name: SIRTOM — Shared composters launch campaign
description: Communication campaign for the launch of shared composters across a public waste authority's territory. The campaign was produced by an agency; I took part in deciding what to brief and ask for, and pushed for a message built on money rather than ecology.
context: Since 1 January 2024, French law requires bio-waste to be sorted at source. To help residents do it, SIRTOM de la région Flers-Condé launched shared composters across its territory, in Normandy, and needed a campaign to announce them.

The campaign was designed and produced by an external agency, not by me. During my internship I took part in the decisions on what to brief the agency on, how to answer its proposals and what to ask for.

work.title: Choosing the angle: savings, not ecology
work.text: I suggested putting the financial side first: the real savings composting brings to the authority, which directly limits increases in the waste collection tax paid by residents.
points: My reading of the audience: the area was not very receptive to environmental messages, and a genuine ecology awareness campaign would need far more time and budget.
So the message had to speak to residents' immediate, practical concerns, starting with their tax bill.

work.title: Working with the agency
work.text: I took part in the back-and-forth with the agency: reviewing its proposals, deciding on the answers and on the requests to send back.

work.title: Where the campaign ran
work.text: The visuals were used across the authority's channels.
points: All of SIRTOM's social media accounts.
The livery of the waste collection trucks that drive across the whole territory.
